title: lexical PDF page markers amplify derived work without a cardinality bound
summary: KCS bounds raw input bytes before indexing but derives PDF page count by counting loose textual `/Page` prefixes. A crafted PDF with one printable stream and many inert `/PageX` markers stays on the deterministic path, pads the page vector to the marker count, and creates one `PreparedUnit` per synthetic page.

codeEvidence.label: Indexing applies a raw byte-size gate
codeEvidence.explanation: The reachable indexing loop rejects files larger than `adapter.policy.max_input_bytes`, but this control is expressed only in raw bytes and does not constrain the number of PDF pages or units later derived from an accepted file.

codeEvidence.label: Accepted content reaches deterministic preparation
codeEvidence.explanation: After passing the byte-size gate, attacker-controlled PDF bytes are read from the indexed scope and forwarded to `prepare_units()` with the file's media type.

codeEvidence.label: Loose `/Page` prefixes define page count
codeEvidence.explanation: `pdf_page_count_in_text()` counts raw textual `/Page` matches in lossy-decoded PDF bytes. A marker such as `/PageX` increments the count because the lookahead excludes `/Pages` but does not require a structural page object or impose a count limit.

codeEvidence.label: Pipeline pads pages to the lexical count
codeEvidence.explanation: For PDF bytes with a text layer, `pdf_text_pages()` trusts the lexical `page_count` and pads the extracted page vector until its length equals that attacker-controlled value.

codeEvidence.label: One `PreparedUnit` is created per padded page
codeEvidence.explanation: `unit_count` is derived from `pdf_pages.len()`, so every padded synthetic page causes additional allocation, hashing, fingerprinting, and an owned `PreparedUnit`.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that parser-derived PDF page cardinality must be structural and bounded before it controls allocation. KCS enforces only a raw byte-size cap, counts loose `/Page` prefixes in attacker-controlled bytes, pads the page vector to that count, and materializes one `PreparedUnit` for each padded entry.

validation.method: static source trace plus bounded local synthetic probe
validation.summary: Source review confirms the byte-size-only control, lexical page count, unbounded page-vector padding, and per-page `PreparedUnit` materialization. The bounded probe reproduced marker counts of 1, 4, 16, and 64 yielding equal page-vector and prepared-unit counts.
assertions: A `/PageX` marker is counted as a page by the reviewed lexical counter.
One printable stream keeps the deterministic PDF path active, so padded empty pages are retained.
Prepared-unit count follows padded page-vector length.
limitations: The unsafe high-marker case was not allocated; the upper range was computed to avoid intentional host exhaustion.
The exact public affected release range and fixing revision were not established in this write-up.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust local content contributor places a crafted PDF in an indexed scope. Normal indexing accepts the file under the raw byte cap, converts inert `/Page`-prefixed tokens into page count, pads the page vector, and allocates/processes one unit per synthetic page. The persistent file can retrigger the condition on later indexing.

dataflow.summary: scope PDF bytes -> `run_index_pipeline()` byte gate -> `prepare_units()` -> `pdf_page_count_in_text()` -> `pdf_text_pages()` padding -> `PreparedUnit` allocation
dataflow.source: attacker-controlled PDF bytes in an indexed local scope
dataflow.sink: `PreparedUnit` vector materialization and associated per-page hashing/fingerprinting
dataflow.outcome: memory and CPU exhaustion of the KCS indexing process

reachability.summary: The attacker needs content-placement ability in a scope the operator indexes; no listener, live service, credentials, or elevated privilege are required.
reachability.entrypoint: ordinary `kcs index` processing of an accepted PDF
preconditions: The PDF begins with `%PDF` and contains enough printable text to avoid the all-garbage OCR fallback.
The operator indexes the affected scope.
reachability.outcome: persistent local denial of service for indexing that scope

impact.why: A small accepted document can drive millions of derived pages and units, exhausting CPU and memory for the local indexing workflow.

likelihood.why: The trigger requires a crafted file, deterministic-path selection, content placement in an indexed scope, and an operator indexing action.

limitations: No code execution, cross-scope corruption, or secret disclosure is shown.
The exact failure threshold depends on host memory, allocator behavior, and surrounding indexing workload.

remediation.summary: Replace loose lexical page counting with structural PDF page counting and enforce a configured derived-page/unit ceiling before `normalize_pdf_page_count()` or `prepare_units()` can allocate per-page objects.
recommendations: Use a PDF parser or validated page tree traversal for page count instead of raw `/Page` substring matching.
Reject, skip, OCR-route, or single-unit degrade PDFs whose structural page count cannot be established safely.
Add a configurable maximum derived PDF page count and enforce it before vector padding.
Carry derived-cardinality budgets through later stages that consume `PreparedUnit` vectors.
regression_tests: A PDF with one printable stream and many `/PageX` markers must not create one unit per marker.
A valid multi-page PDF under the configured limit should still produce expected page units.
A valid PDF above the derived-page limit should fail in a controlled skip/error path.
A textless PDF should continue to use the existing OCR fallback.
A boundary test should combine the raw byte cap with the derived page limit.
